messages:
alba: FYI I'm going to enable a short canary for the new consent-stamp debug logs on the router for 30m. want to validate debounce across bursty chat routes.
jo: what's the exact goal here? is this to verify we don't double-log the same consent token during retries? :thinking_face:
alba: exactly. earlier we saw duplicate inspect events when clients retried. debounce should collapse duplicates for 1min window by default so we don't double-count and avoid PII leakage.
matt: key questions: where do we store the stamp? raw stamp in logs is a no-go. we need a k-anonymized fingerprint (hmac) and TTL + no full-text storage.
samir: agree. propose header X-Consent-Stamp that we hash server-side with tenant salt. we should document salt rotation impact on dedupe.
jo: also need to think sampling unit — per-tenant vs per-route. per-tenant reduces noise for big customers but hides route-level regressions. per-route catches regression but can blow up costs.
alba: my canary: per-route for 5% traffic for 30m, but we hash stamp and only log the hmac. retention set to 14 days for canary. if looks good, expand to per-tenant 1% baseline + per-route spike capture.
matt: can we add a cheap metric instead of full logs? e.g., emit counters: consent_debounced_count, consent_unique_hmac_count. then logs only when consent_debounced_count increases by anomalous delta.
samir: +1. counters feed dashboard alerts and keep raw payloads out of storage. will need an aggregation key — use (tenant_id, route, model_shard).
alba: example config i'm going to flip in route config: 
```
consent_logging: 
  enabled: true
  mode: canary
  traffic_pct: 5
  debounce_ms: 60000
  emit_counters_only: true
  store_raw_stamp: false
  stamp_hash_alg: HMAC-SHA256
  retention_days: 14
```
jo: small nit: `emit_counters_only` might stop us from troubleshooting edgecases where we need a sample of stamped requests. can we support 'counters_plus_sample_n' where n=10 per 10k requests?
matt: yep. add `sample_rate: 0.001` or `sample_n: 10` so ops can fetch a handful of hashed stamps for replay. ensure those samples are kept encrypted in audit bucket.
samir: also need a runtime toggle in the console for rollout UX: a single slider with breakdown: canary % / sample rate / retention. product asked for simple controls.
alba: agree. ops wants fine-grain control too. plan: console will expose quick presets: minimal, canary, debug. default minimal=emit_counters_only true, sample_rate=0.0001. debug=emit_raw=false but sample_rate=0.01 and retention 7 days.
jo: alerting: add a heatmap on dashboard showing consent_unique_hmac_count / minute per route. spike detection triggers an ops paging rule if > X% rise in 5m.
matt: quota concerns: if we accidentally enable debug on a chatty route we could drown storage. Gate it behind a per-tenant logging budget and enforce hard stop. also surface estimated token+storage cost in console prior to flip.
alba: i'll add a preflight estimate: expected_rps * avg_event_size -> cost estimate. console should warn if budget exceeded.
samir: we should also record provenance metadata (who toggled, commit sha, timestamp) in the audit log for compliance.
deploy-bot: deploy: consent-stamp-canary toggled for route /chat/stream on canary-5pct at 2026-03-21T16:02:15Z :rocket:
alba: Thanks. I'll watch metrics for 30m. tagging @oncall for visibility. :eyes:
jo: if we see >2x duplicates or any PII leakage in the sample, rollback immediately. keep rollback playbook ready.
matt: one more internal-api debate: current router header is `x-redwood-consent` — should we standardize to `x-consent-stamp` to be vendor neutral? impacts SDKs.
samir: worth thinking about long-term; add deprecation header mapping for one release.
alba: ok plan summary: 5% per-route canary, hashed stamps only, counters + tiny sampling, console preset UX, preflight cost estimate, per-tenant budget hard stop, audit provenance. rolling for 30m then meet. :+1:
